usable: yes for P1 (same rows, published rule for exclusions, published model). No P2: single-lab data, no source column. Their exact split cannot be reproduced (see bar.exact_split).

source.paper: Ma W., ..., Song N., Ding P. J. Mater. Inform. 5 (2025), doi:10.20517/jmi.2025.09 (Shanghai University), CC BY 4.0

target: LOI (%), polypropylene + halogen-free FR composites (iteration 1 of their active-learning loop)

rows.exclusions (theirs, label-free): their 2-of-3 outlier vote on standardised features only (IsolationForest(contamination=0.05, random_state=8585), OneClassSVM(nu=0.05, kernel='rbf', gamma='scale'), LocalOutlierFactor(n_neighbors=2, contamination=0.05)); fitted on all 227 rows' features, LOI never read. Fixed list computed 2026-10-07 with sklearn 1.7.1: No = [3, 18, 27, 32, 33, 34, 40, 42, 46, 54].
rows.assert_before_any_fit: re-running the rule gives exactly that list and 217 rows; otherwise BLOCKED.
rows.sensitivity: P1 is also run on all 227 rows (no exclusion) and reported next to it, never selected on and never the claim (pre-split outlier removal flatters test R2; lit_loi.md methods table).

features: the 30 mass-fraction columns of Data_LOI.xlsx (all columns except 'No' and 'LOI'), file order.

bar.set: test set of one random 4:1 split, iteration 1, Ridge(alpha=0.1)
bar.quote_protocol: "After outlier deletion, the preprocessed data were randomly split as training set and test set according to the ratio 4:1."
bar.quote_result: "when alpha was set to 0.1, the model shows outstanding robustness (R2 of 0.945 for LOOCV) and commendable generalization ability (R2 of 0.919 for the test set)."
bar.where_read: full text, OA HTML https://www.oaepublish.com/articles/jmi.2025.09 (Methods 'Data collection and preprocessing', 'Model establishment and selection'; Results 'Interpretable Ridge models construction').
bar.best_model: Ridge(alpha=0.1) after StandardScaler, chosen for interpretability over SVR/XGBoost/GBR/RF; LOOCV R2 on the training set: SVR 0.907, XGBoost 0.942, GBR 0.958, RF 0.956, Ridge 0.944 (0.945 after tuning).
bar.exact_split: not reproducible. Code '2.Algorithm comparison.py' draws seed = np.random.randint(2000, 3000); the comment records '#RGRandomseed 2323' for Ridge, and the split uses the authors' own package (fml.sampling.random_split(percent=0.2)), which was not released. So no P1_pub.
not_a_bar: LOOCV-on-train R2 0.945: printed for context (P1 also reports LOOCV R2 on each training part for r0 only).
Mean of 100 random 4:1 splits (Fig. 2C): the value appears only in a figure, not read; the text says it 'closely resemble[s]' the single-split result.
Iteration-2 test R2 0.939: the iteration-2 training data are not released.

r0 (reproduction control): StandardScaler() fit on the training part -> Ridge(alpha=0.1) (code '3.Model optimization.py' and '7. Model stability validation.py').
reproduction_gate: no exact split exists, so the gate is r0's P1 mean in [0.889, 0.949] (bar +- 0.03, from their statement that the 100-split mean closely resembles 0.919). Outside -> FLAG 'Ma protocol not reproduced', no P1 sentence.

protocols.P1: train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=s), s = 0..9, on the 217 rows; StandardScaler inside the training part for r0 (c1-c3 per common). Test R2 (primary), RMSE, MAE. Same splits on the 227-row sensitivity set use the same seeds.
protocols.P2: not possible: no source-paper column (data from the group's own earlier work plus new experiments).

notes: Single matrix (PP), 30 composition features, 217 rows: a linear model is near-optimal here; expect c1-c3 to be close to r0 and all near 0.9. This dataset tests Dravix on narrow, single-lab data, not under its harder protocol.
c2 (TabPFN v2) is well inside its limits here (173 training rows, 30 features).
